methods.label: Find the row endings
methods.explanation:
The centered rows contain \(1,3,5,7,\ldots\) consecutive numbers. Counting the top row as row \(1\), row \(r\) therefore contains \(2r-1\) numbers.

The total number of entries through row \(r\) is \(r^2\). To see why, imagine growing a square of dots from size \((r-1)\times(r-1)\) to size \(r\times r\). The new bottom row and right column add \(r+(r-1)=2r-1\) dots, exactly the next row length in the array. Thus row \(r\) ends with \(r^2\).

Since
\[
11^2=121<142\leq144=12^2,
\]
\(142\) is in row \(12\), whose last entry is \(144\). Row \(11\) ends with \(121\) and extends one space less far to the right, so \(121\) is directly above \(143\). Moving one space left gives \(\boxed{120}\) directly above \(142\), choice \(\text{C}\).
